- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:10209-10226 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash, anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: In heal_stale_decision, the last run relaxed the cut-short-page coverage gate from `if not reaches_anchor and not page_complete:` to `if not reaches_anchor and not page_complete and len(window) < green_runs:`. A page that misses older runs can now close the issue when it holds at least `green_runs` post-anchor green runs, and a failed post-anchor push run older than the fetched page is never seen by the `conclusion != "success"` check.
  WHY: On a busy branch where `total_count > per_page`, the issue closes as `workflow_green` while a post-anchor failure exists. The re-anchor via occurrence comment depends on the intake correlating the recurrence and on the occurrence POST succeeding, and the locking test was rewritten to `test_heal_stale_runs_page_cut_short_closes_only_with_enough_green_runs`. Severity disagreement: gemini=BLOCKER, minimax/luna/glm=MAJOR, sonnet=NIT (sonnet calls it an accepted design trade-off: the linked issue specifies a single `per_page=<HEAL_STALE_GREEN_RUNS+10>` read, and the stricter rule could never close #8352). The highest is used.
- changelog.d/8808-heal-stale-auto-close.md:2 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The changelog still says the issue "closes as completed when its workflow has passed on every completed push run on the target branch since the issue was last reported". The close comment, the agents.d fragment and the docstring were all updated to the cut-short-page rule; the changelog was not.
  WHY: This is documentation drift only. The release notes tell operators that a closed issue had no failure since its anchor, which the code no longer guarantees. Both reviewers rated it NIT; z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised the same item as a hardening suggestion.

  WHY: The lint aggregate stays red until the failing test is identified from the full job log. The editor should pull the full log before changing code.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- changelog.d/8808-heal-stale-auto-close.md:line 2 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The changelog still claims every push run since the anchor passed. The relaxed gate (`if not reaches_anchor and not page_complete and len(window) < green_runs:`) can close the issue on a cut-short page, and the close comment and agents.d fragment were updated to match but the changelog was not.
  WHY: This is documentation only, but a closed issue can contradict the release note on a busy branch. Suggested fix: "passed on each of the newest completed push runs on the target branch since the issue was last reported (at least HEAL_STALE_GREEN_RUNS of them)".
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:heal_stale_decision, `if not reaches_anchor and not page_complete and len(window) < green_runs: return done("keep", "runs_window_incomplete")` | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Post-anchor runs older than the page are never seen, so a failure among them does not stop the close. The reviewer assesses this as an accepted design trade-off.
  WHY: A same-fingerprint recurrence posts an occurrence comment that re-anchors (workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:101, workflow_failure_heal.py:7942, check at 10183). The residual remains only when the occurrence POST failed or the fingerprint differs. The issue specifies a single `per_page=<HEAL_STALE_GREEN_RUNS+10>` read, and the stricter rule could never close #8352. No change recommended beyond an optional comment sentence.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:(CI check-run "orchestrate-poll (2)", run 42813136022, job 129819345158) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The shard failed on a12d0f1c with no visible FAIL line. The `##[error] Integration fingerprint verification FAILED` lines are expected output of a test that passes. test_complete_verdict_falls_through_to_finalize_on_integration_drift (baseline_timeout shard) is unverified.
  WHY: The failing test name must be found in the full job log. The last-run mock additions are opt-in.
- HARDENING: changelog.d/8808-heal-stale-auto-close.md line 2: reword the coverage claim (1 line). scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py comment above the runs_window_incomplete gate: add one sentence on the failed-occurrence-POST residual (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1 (2 related items)

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:10219-10223 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cut-short-page gate (`if not reaches_anchor and not page_complete and len(window) < green_runs:`) keeps the issue only when there are fewer than `green_runs` post-anchor runs.
  WHY: A truncated page that holds `green_runs` or more successes closes the issue even if an older run outside the page failed. The gate must be `if not reaches_anchor and not page_complete: return done("keep", "runs_window_incomplete")`, or it must verify page coverage explicitly.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:heal_stale_decision, run-coverage guard `if not reaches_anchor and not page_complete and len(window) < green_runs:` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The guard allows a close on a cut-short page that holds at least `green_runs` post-anchor runs. This deviates from the spec, which requires the page to reach the anchor or hold every run in `total_count` and otherwise keeps the issue as `runs_window_incomplete`. The test was rewritten to `test_heal_stale_runs_page_cut_short_closes_only_with_enough_green_runs`.
  WHY: When `total_count > per_page`, an older post-anchor failure outside the page is invisible to the `run_not_green` check, so the issue closes as `workflow_green`. A single transient failure that does not recur leaves the issue closed without the plan ever being implemented.
- changelog.d/8808-heal-stale-auto-close.md:line 2 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The changelog describes the pre-relaxation rule, while the agents.d fragment and the docstring describe the cut-short-page rule.
  WHY: This is documentation drift only. Operators triaging a closed issue from the release notes will draw the wrong conclusion.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:10219-10223 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A truncated runs page is accepted whenever it holds at least `green_runs` post-anchor runs, even when `total_count` confirms that older runs were omitted.
  WHY: Only the returned runs are checked. For example, a page of 15 successful runs with `total_count` > 15 passes the guard while an omitted post-anchor failure goes unseen. This violates the requirement that every completed push run after the anchor succeed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:10209-10226 (the gate at 10219 changed by the last run; success check at 10222) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The last run weakened the gate from `if not reaches_anchor and not page_complete:` to `... and len(window) < green_runs:`. A failed post-anchor run older than the fetched page is invisible to the `conclusion != "success"` check at line 10222. The comment's re-anchor rationale (10213-10215) depends on the intake correlating the recurrence and on the occurrence post succeeding. The locking test was replaced, so the premature-close path is untested.
  WHY: A long-held heal issue on a busy branch (the #8352 case) closes on the first green newest page despite an older post-anchor failure. The close comment and the changelog both claim a stronger guarantee, and the close can only be undone through the unreliable recurrence path.

(at least `HEAL_STALE_GREEN_RUNS` of them)" (1 line, risk 1). scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py 10209-10215 comment: note that a cut-short-page close can miss an older post-anchor failure, recovered only when the intake files the next generation (2 lines, risk 2). (2 related items)
